A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAMM research work. All 19 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison through readable text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original C4 pretraining, GLUE finetuning, compression ablations, and activation/gradient analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original pretraining and finetuning results and additionally reports runtime measurements, pretraining uncertainty, and training-stability results.

M1.justification: The core sampling, scaled representatives, and gradient approximation are retained. However, v2 Algorithm 1 uses signed cosine argmax and an absolute residual threshold, whereas v1 uses distance minimization and relative error, also required by v2 Lemma 1 and Equation 2. The PDFs do not resolve whether these differences are intended procedural changes or pseudocode errors.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate C4 language-model pretraining and the same eight GLUE tasks. The new timing and stability studies introduce no additional dataset, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: Full training remains the reference, and Figure 4 retains CompAct and Uniform-CRS, labeled Uniform in the plot. New timing and loss comparisons reuse the full-training baseline. ESPACE is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 Section 4.4 adds a substantive efficiency-evaluation protocol: single-GPU timing with 16K tokens per batch, averaged over 1000 iterations, at r=1/512 across three model sizes, plus forward/backward operation timing per 1K tokens. The existing pretraining and finetuning budgets, batch sizes, learning-rate searches, and task metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds Appendix G/Figure 8 to examine optimization stability using baseline and PAMM loss trajectories, plus a forward/backward runtime decomposition in Table 2b. Existing compression-ratio and epsilon ablations and the PCA, approximation-error, and coverage analyses in Figures 4–7 are retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports three-run pretraining averages, adds uncertainty entries in Table 3 and error bars in Figure 3, and displays three seed-specific PAMM loss curves. v1 provides pretraining point estimates without a run count. GLUE's three-seed averaging is unchanged. The statistic represented by the new plus/minus values is not explicitly defined.

E6.justification: All nine PAMM pretraining estimates change between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 3; for example, the 1B result at r=1/512 changes from 15.10 to 15.36 ± 0.04. v1 Figure 3 instead plots approximately 16.1 for that entry, revealing an earlier reporting inconsistency. v2 adds throughput degradation of 19.74%, 11.71%, and 2.67% for 60M, 350M, and 1B, respectively, and new stability findings. GLUE scores, existing memory measurements, and Figures 4–7 results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds the absolute-cosine assignment lemma and its proof, and extends the retained coverage theorem with an argument presented as proving approximately constant b/n_min. It removes v1's explicit memory/time complexity and speedup derivations. Equation 5's retention-probability factor is corrected, and the approximation bound replaces the Frobenius norm of B with its spectral norm.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: PAMM exploits token redundancy to compress QKV activations by up to 512-fold while preserving comparable model quality and compatibility with efficient attention. Added runtime and stability evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v1 anticipates substantial speedups from an optimized CUDA implementation; v2 interprets measured overhead as small and concludes that custom kernels would offer only marginal benefit. v2 also adds an inference of stable optimization. It removes the explicit untested-large-model limitation and isotropic curse-of-dimensionality discussion, while adding qualifications concerning dependence and minimum-neighborhood scaling.

D1.justification: v2 documents vectorized row-norm, cosine-similarity, masking, and index_add operations in its rewritten pseudocode. A new reproducibility statement claims downloadable source code in supplementary materials, although availability cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs. Existing training hyperparameters and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds ESPACE and distinguishes its inference-oriented compression objective from PAMM's training-memory objective. It sharpens the comparison with CompAct and removes the Banerjee et al. and Vershynin citations accompanying deleted theoretical discussion. Abbreviated author lists otherwise retain the same cited works.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and method explanation undergo extensive sentence and paragraph rewriting. Related-work subsections become paragraph headings, the method exposition is reorganized, pseudocode moves from the final appendix to Appendix A, and the experimental appendices are reordered. A reproducibility statement is added and the standalone limitations section disappears.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn, and Figure 3 changes from a perplexity-versus-memory plot to separate grouped bar charts with error bars and compression annotations. v2 adds runtime Table 2 and loss Figure 8 and adopts the ICLR layout. Existing Figures 4–7 retain their graphics, but Figure 6's new subcaptions incorrectly swap the epsilon and compression-ratio descriptions.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies measured runtime where v1 offered theoretical speedup discussion, and adds repeated-run pretraining uncertainty and loss trajectories. These changes improve assessment of practical cost and stability. The net gain is limited by new pseudocode inconsistencies, insufficient justification of minimum-neighborhood scaling, and removal of the explicit model-scale limitation.
